newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican farm group to open agricultural stores.
newsitem.headline: Mexican farm group to open agricultural stores.

text.p: The National Association of Horticultural Exporters and Growers plans to open a series of agricultural produce supermarkets by the second quarter of 1997, the president of the group said Tuesday.
Enrique Ruelas Vallejo said in an interview that the stores will form part of a new sales drive by the national farm group based here to open new sales outlets for members.
He said it is part of a wider pyramidal distribution drive to get products from the field to people's mouths without using intermediaries.

Ruelas Vallejo said government plans to boost production would fall flat if new sales opportunities were also not opened up. "We need sales support just as much as production support," he said, explaining the supermarket move.

Plans are to cut out middlemen in the direct sale of between 10 to 15 products at the outset, with a target of 50 products for the future. "A total of 50 products would be ideal, but we do not have 50 products to offer right now," he said.
Ruelas Vallejo said the idea is to concession the stores and to supply them from a central base where growers will deliver products.
